b635514d4a5edacf: KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd's net profit dropped 3.8 per cent to RM1.77 billion in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), from RM1.84 billion a year earlier, mainly due to higher loan impairment allowances.
Public Bank said the lower profit was mainly attributed to a RM116.4 million increase in loan and financing impairment allowances following the normalisation of credit charges.
Investment income also declined by RM90.8 million, while other operating expenses rose 3.7 per cent, or RM47 million.

"These were partially mitigated by RM75.8 million (9.5 per cent) increase in net fee and other income, mainly driven by higher unit trust related fee income and bancassurance income, and RM73.5 million (2.6 per cent) increase in net interest and Islamic banking income," it said.

Public Bank also suffered from higher other comprehensive losses of RM385.5 million to RM451 million, mainly attributable to higher losses on revaluation of financial investments arising from higher market yields on bonds, partially mitigated by gains from the translation of foreign operations.
Despite the challenging environment, the banking group's revenue rose 4.4 per cent year on year to RM7.74 billion from RM7.42 billion, according to its bourse filing.
Its gross impaired loans ratio remained stable at 0.55 per cent as at Sept 30, 2026, below the industry average of 1.42 per cent.
Malaysia's third-largest bank by assets did not declare a dividend for the quarter, bringing its total dividend paid for the financial year so far to 22.5 sen per share.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Public Bank's net profit was largely unchanged at RM5.35 billion from a year earlier, while revenue increased to RM22.67 billion from RM22.08 billion.
Public Bank said Malaysia's banking sector remains resilient despite a more challenging operating environment, supported by ample liquidity and strong capital buffers.
"The Public Bank group will continue to uphold its commitment to further strengthen its role as a financial intermediary in support of national development.
"The group will continue to prioritise prudence in the management of credit risk, uphold strong corporate governance and ensure effective risk management to safeguard stakeholder value," it said.
On a segmental basis, pre-tax profit decreased across all segments, except for fund management and head office, funding centre and others.
Corporate lending's pre-tax profit fell 29.5 per cent to RM163.2 million, mainly due to lower net writeback of loan/financing impairment allowance.
Hire purchase's pre-tax profit fell 23 per cent to RM114.4 million mainly due to higher loans/financing impairment allowance, lower net interest/financing income and higher other operating expenses.

Treasury and capital market operations also saw a 45 per cent drop in pre-tax profit during the quarter to RM47.2 million, mainly due to lower investment income arising from rising market yields on bonds.
Investment banking saw 39.2 per cent lower pre-tax profit to RM11.7 million, mainly due to lower investment income and corporate advisory fee income.

On the other hand, fund management's profit increased by 11.6 per cent to RM246.9 million, mainly due to higher management fee from higher average net asset value of funds and higher fee on sale of trust units.

Head office, funding centre and other segments recorded 27.1 per cent higher profit during the quarter to RM387.5 million, mainly due to higher net interest/financing income from funding and investment activities, partially offset by lower investment income and higher other operating expenses.

f47eca3d4b47131a: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has criticised opposition lawmakers for remaining silent over alleged multibillion-ringgit losses linked to Sabah gas projects dating back to 2016.
He said the two pipeline projects had resulted in losses of RM9 billion, although RM5 billion had since been recovered through a loan restructuring agreement with China.
"We managed to recover RM5 billion," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Taman Kosas in Ampang.
He challenged opposition lawmakers for failing to raise the matter in Parliament despite the scale of the alleged losses.
"I have yet to see the opposition debate this in Parliament," he said.
Anwar also questioned whether the opposition considered the losses acceptable and referred to losses involving Felda and Tabung Haji.
He accused political leaders of focusing on racial issues while overlooking corruption and financial misconduct.
"We keep talking about race, but we allow corruption to continue. What kind of politics is this? It is immature," he said.
Anwar said political discourse should instead focus on national development, accountability and efforts to combat corruption.
"We keep talking about race, but we allow corruption to continue. What kind of politics is this? It is immature," he said.

On Tuesday, Anwar told the Dewan Rakyat that Malaysia had reduced its losses from two failed pipeline projects from RM8 billion to RM3 billion after reaching a RM5 billion loan restructuring agreement with China.
He said RM8.3 billion, or 88 per cent of the projects' combined RM9.4 billion contract value, had been paid by 2018, despite reported construction progress of only 13 per cent.
The projects, comprising the Trans-Sabah Gas Pipeline and Multi-Product Pipeline, were awarded through direct negotiations in 2016 and terminated in 2018.
Anwar also said investigations were ongoing and elements of corruption had been detected, although authorities faced difficulties obtaining information involving China.
f292c2afe1580b92: KUALA LUMPUR: French Open champions Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun produced a stunning second-game comeback to reach the Korea Open men's doubles semi-finals in Yeosu today, moving another step closer to back-to-back World Tour titles.
The world No. 9 defeated Japan's Haruki Kawabe-Kenta Matsukawa 21-14, 26-24 in a thrilling quarter-final that saw them survive five game points in the second game.
After comfortably taking the opener, Wei Chong-Kai Wun found themselves trailing 18-11 in the second before staging a remarkable fightback to force a tense finish.
The third seeds eventually prevailed 26-24 to extend their winning streak to eight matches, having captured the Super 750 French Open title in Paris less than two weeks ago.

Wei Chong-Kai Wun will next face the winners of the quarter-final between South Korea's world No. 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae and China's eighth seeds Wang Chang-Xie Hao Nan for a place in Sunday's final.
7440ac9f8ab829ee: BATU GAJAH: After nearly four years apart from his family, a former inmate had just one wish upon his early release today — to seek his mother's forgiveness.

The man, who wished to be known only as Thilagan, 36, from Teluk Intan, said the royal pardon granted by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, in conjunction with the ruler's official birthday celebration was an opportunity to mend his relationship with his family.
"I want to hold my mother's feet first and apologise to her because I have hurt her feelings so many times.

"I realise that I have made many mistakes, been a bad son and often caused my family worry, but now I want to change," he said after the early release ceremony at the Batu Gajah Correctional Centre here today.
Thilagan was among 58 prospects in Perak released before the expiry of their prison sentences after receiving pardons granted by Sultan Nazrin on the recommendation of the Perak Pardons Board.
Deputy Commissioner-General of Prisons (Security and Correctional) Rosoman Abu Bakar @ Che Din officiated the ceremony.
Thilagan said his release would allow him to celebrate his mother's 73rd birthday on Dec 8, as well as Deepavali with his family.

"It has been a long time since I last ate my mother's cooking. When I called her yesterday, she said she would prepare vegetable curry and stingray sambal. I am also looking forward to eating mutton curry," he said.
Thilagan had been serving a three-year-and-three-month prison sentence for an offence under Section 39C of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Another inmate granted early release, Yugan, 33, from Tapah, said his nearly four years behind bars had taught him to improve himself and avoid repeating past mistakes.
He said he had acquired various skills, alongside religious knowledge, which he hoped would serve as a foundation for a new life.
"I want to change and never return to prison again. During my time here, I have learnt a lot, including religious knowledge, marching drills and sewing skills at the workshop," he said.
Along, 28, from Kuala Kangsar, said he did not want to blame anyone for his involvement in drug abuse.

He was initially due for release in January 2027 after being detained in 2023. He said his parents advised him to seek employment away from his hometown to avoid environments that could lead him back to his old habits.
"I do not want to blame anyone or point fingers at my friends because the decision to get involved with drugs was entirely my own.
"I hope to secure a job after my release. Once I have a job and a more stable life, I also hope to start a family of my own," he said.
He said that during his sentence, he had also acquired event management skills, including setting up tents and tables, which he hoped would help him secure employment. — BERNAMA
0f2dfa49b70ca26d: PETALING JAYA: CelcomDigi Bhd has reduced its operational and purchased-electricity emissions by 3.95 per cent between 2024 and 2025 as it stepped up energy efficiency measures across its telecommunications network.
The company also recorded a 30 per cent reduction in carbon emissions per terabyte of data consumed between 2023 and 2025, despite growing demand for data services.
CelcomDigi said more than 15,000 network sites are equipped with energy-saving features as part of its five-year environmental, social and governance (ESG) roadmap.

Its head of sustainability Philip Ling said the company expects further reductions in carbon emissions through the adoption of energy-efficient technologies, including artificial intelligence, across its network infrastructure.
"One of our biggest initiatives this year has been improving energy efficiency, particularly through the use of AI in our networks.
"Our network towers can now enter different sleep modes, including micro-sleep and hibernation, to reduce energy consumption.

"We expect to see further reductions in carbon emissions. From last year to this year, we have achieved a 3.95 per cent reduction, and we hope to maintain this downward trend every year," he told reporters after CelcomDigi's Responsible Business Day 2026.
Beyond environmental sustainability, Ling said the company has also made progress in digital safety, supply chain sustainability and governance under its ESG roadmap.
CelcomDigi currently flags about 260 million suspected scam calls and blocks 22 million SMS messages monthly, while its Online Safety IRL 2.0 initiative has recorded 22.3 million views.
On supply chain sustainability, the company is on track to meet its annual commitments of 25,000 supplier training hours and 800 supplier inspections to strengthen responsible business practices.
Ling said CelcomDigi has also established a Responsible AI Governance Framework to strengthen transparency, accountability and data protection across its operations and services.
"It is an ongoing journey, again, aligned very much to where the government and regulators are guiding us," he said.

1dae0119f60be0b5: KUALA SELANGOR: The Selangor government will order a review of previously approved development projects to ensure that flood mitigation systems are implemented in high-risk areas.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said this measure is part of the state government's efforts to reduce flood risks and prevent a recurrence of such incidents in the affected areas.

"I will request a review of all approvals we have granted, including imposing a requirement for developers to construct temporary water retention facilities; we certainly do not want them to carry out the work in a shoddy or substandard manner," he said when met after inspecting a retention pond site at the Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Puncak Alam campus here today.
Amirudin added that the state government has also identified several other issues contributing to flooding in areas such as Johan Setia, Parit Mahang, Bukit Kuching, and Bukit Hijau.

He saId identified issues include acts of vandalism along the embankments of the Sungai Buloh 1 Flood Mitigation Scheme where the structures have been lowered below their original specifications as well as water overflow originating from the West Coast Expressway (WCE).
"I have requested that the vandalism issue be addressed immediately. We will take action against illegal operations in the area, and several demolition exercises will have to be carried out.

"These demolitions are necessary to gazette the sites as water catchment areas or floodplains two locations have already been identified for this purpose. The process will be executed by the District and Land Office in collaboration with the local authorities," he said.

Meanwhile, addressing the case of a mosque that frequently experiences flooding despite not being situated near a river, Amirudin noted that his administration would consult with the mosque's management to discuss either raising the structure or relocating the place of worship to a more suitable site.
He said this occurs because the area is low-lying and receives overflow from the Subang River.

"This is overflow from the Subang River, which flows toward Merbau Sempak, eventually reaching the Sungai Buloh river system and arriving here. Ultimately, the water seeks an outlet to the sea but there is no sea here so the nearest coastline is in Kuala Selangor.

"This has long been the natural movement of water; runoff from Gombak or Petaling tends to flow toward the Ijok or Kuala Selangor areas and this has been the established pattern for a long time," he said.
2539072fe1bae843: ISTANBUL: Turkey's parliament ratified a regional defence pact involving Saudi Arabia and Pakistan overnight, state media reported.
The three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August, committing them to come to one another's aid if any member is attacked.
The pact links Nato member Turkey, which has the alliance's second-largest army, with Pakistan, the Islamic world's only nuclear-armed state, and Saudi Arabia, the Gulf's leading power.
Lawmakers approved the measure by 279 votes to 119, according to the state-run Anadolu news agency.

During parliamentary debates, ruling AKP lawmaker Ziya Altunyaldiz said the agreement was not directed against any third country and was intended to prevent conflicts rather than escalate them, Anadolu reported.
Saudi Arabia has faced repeated attacks by Yemen's Huthi rebels targeting cities, oil facilities and shipping since fighting in the impoverished country's civil war intensified again in July.
4f9b1820452c6a7c: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has upheld the High Court's decision to recognise a former production director as an employee of the company and ruling that he was unfairly dismissed.

A three-member panel chaired by Justice Azhahari Kamal Ramli unanimously upheld the High Court's award of RM492,000 in back wages, equivalent to 24 months of the late V Rajkumar's salary and allowances.
However, the final sum payable was RM472,000 after deducting RM20,000.

The panel, which included Justices Ahmad Kamal Shahid and Latifah Tahar, also allowed the appeal by the company, Suntech Engineering Korea Co Ltd, to set aside the additional RM50,000 awarded as punitive compensation.
In delivering the decision, Azhahari said Rajkumar's evidence regarding his appointment had not been rebutted by the company's material witness.
He noted that the company had also failed to call the witness to testify and said the evidence presented was sufficient to establish its liability.

The dispute arose after Rajkumar, who was appointed director of production in May 2019 at a monthly salary of RM20,000 plus a RM500 petrol allowance, was denied access to his workplace at the Lumut shipyard on Oct 1, 2019.
He subsequently pursued an unfair dismissal claim under the Industrial Relations Act 1967.
The Industrial Court dismissed his claim in August 2024 on the ground that he had failed to establish an employment relationship with the company.
Rajkumar successfully challenged the Industrial Court's decision through a judicial review application, and the High Court overturned the ruling last year.
He died four months ago while the company's appeal against the High Court's decision was pending. His widow, V Prema Devi, was subsequently appointed to continue the proceedings on his behalf.
R Jayabalan and S Siva Nantha appeared for Prema, while Donovan Cheah and Ilyssa Jace Chakrabarty represented the company.
91b69ba816756f74: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian para bowling has entered a new chapter under the Malaysian Tenpin Bowling Congress (MTBC), with more than 100 bowlers from 12 contingents taking part in the inaugural National Para Interstate Championships, which saw Selangor crowned overall champions.

The three-day competition, which concluded at Sunway Mega Lanes in Subang Jaya on Wednesday marked an important milestone for MTBC, which assumed responsibility for para bowling from the Paralympic Council Malaysia (PCM) in October last year.
Selangor emerged comfortable winners with eight gold, four silver and four bronze medals, ahead of Penang (3-1-2) and Sabah (2-1-1).
MTBC secretary-general Maradona Chok said the championship reflected the congress' commitment to providing para bowlers with the same development opportunities as their able-bodied counterparts.

"Since taking over the para bowling portfolio and officially becoming a member of PCM, we have a responsibility to ensure that para bowlers receive the same attention and opportunities as able-bodied athletes," said Maradona.
"Our president, Datuk Mohammed Najeeb Abdullah, made it clear that we must do for para bowling what we have been doing for able-bodied bowling.
"He was very firm that we should introduce the para interstate championship as soon as possible. That was why we made it a priority to get the competition started this year."
Maradona was also encouraged by the response, with 12 contingents participating and 11 returning home with at least one medal.
"For an inaugural championship, the turnout from the states has been very encouraging. It is a good starting point for us," he said.
On the lanes, Selangor's Rosheedey Faizal was among three bowlers who captured two gold medals.
Rosheedey won the men's TPB8 (wheelchair) singles before combining with Ahmad Nazri Hamzah to claim the TPB8+8 doubles title.
Sabah's Mohamad Azri Azman also completed a double, winning the men's TPB3 (visual impairment) singles and partnering Azuan Amir Hassan to victory in the TPB1+3 doubles.
Selangor's Mohd Amin Abd Rashid was another double gold medallist, triumphing in the men's TPB10 (upper limb impairment) singles before joining Mohd Fauzi Ghazalli to win the TPB10+10 doubles.
729d4be452ffc540: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Barely 4 per cent of Malaysians feel their smartphones are genuinely secure against hackers and scammers, according to a survey by digital wealth platform Versa, published just days before the annual 11.11 shopping blitz.
The survey of 1,022 local users revealed that 78 per cent had crossed paths with a scam over the preceding two years, either falling victim themselves or seeing family and acquaintances targeted.

Among the 798 respondents who encountered these rackets, nearly three in four pointed to their mobile phones as the primary point of contact. Direct phone calls and SMS messages proved the most persistent channels, cited by 80 per cent of affected respondents, while messaging apps trailed closely behind at 76 per cent.

Versa warned that syndicates deliberately exploit the fast-paced frenzy of year-end flash sales and bogus parcel delivery texts. Rushed buyers frequently tap dubious tracking links or surrender personal banking credentials without second thought.

The survey findings align with grim data from federal police. Bukit Aman’s Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) reported that online crime almost doubled in 2025, topping 66,000 cases and draining RM2.97 billion from victims nationwide.

That momentum has barely slowed in 2026. Police tracked 16,880 online scams siphoning more than RM555.7 million in the first quarter alone, including 4,858 cases tied to e-commerce fraud. During the first half of the year, another 5,134 QR-code fraud cases bled RM28.67 million from consumers.

To safeguard shoppers ahead of the 11.11 sales, Versa outlined several critical precautions. Consumers should first verify unfamiliar recipient bank accounts and phone numbers on the police’s Semak Mule portal before making any direct funds transfer.
Purchases should remain strictly within established e-commerce platforms, with any seller request to switch to WhatsApp or pay via manual bank transfer treated as an immediate red flag.

Shoppers must also resist artificial urgency, such as countdown timers and low-stock alerts designed to rush buyers past basic security checks. Sensitive credentials, including OTPs, TAC codes, and banking passwords, should never be disclosed, as legitimate merchants and courier services will never ask for them.

When considering financial products, consumers must verify that the platform holds a valid licence using the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) Investment Checker, ensuring the firm does not appear on the SC Investor Alert List. In the event of a suspected breach, victims should act swiftly by freezing their accounts through bank fraud desks, contacting the National Scam Response Centre at 997, and filing an official police report.
“This sale season, the strongest financial defence is simply taking a five-second pause to double-check where your money is actually going,” Versa chief executive and co-founder Teoh Wei Xiang said.
The fintech platform has also rolled out an educational video starring brand ambassador Khairy Jamaluddin, featuring a dramatised encounter with an operative from a scam syndicate.
Versa noted that the 4 per cent security confidence score and the 78 per cent exposure rate originate from an in-app survey conducted among its registered user base in February 2025.

Because the dataset relies on self-reported answers from platform members collected over 18 months ago, the findings provide an indicative snapshot rather than an exhaustive representation of the entire Malaysian population.

Taufiq berkata, acara kecergasan massa seperti itu wajar diteruskan untuk menggalakkan gaya hidup aktif dan sihat dalam kalangan rakyat Malaysia.
Sebelum ini, beliau berkata, KBS tidak akan meluluskan penganjuran acara Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 sekiranya tajaan syarikat minuman beralkohol tidak ditarik balik sepenuhnya.

a400539f2462abbc: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Cabinet has agreed to a memorandum on amendments to the Borneo States (Legislative Powers) Order for Sarawak, paving the way for the transfer of scheduled waste management powers to the state government under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).

Madani government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the memorandum, submitted by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), was agreed upon at today’s Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the proposed amendments had received clearance from the Attorney-General’s Chambers and would next be submitted for royal consent from His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.

“This decision reflects the Prime Minister’s and government’s commitment to strengthening the implementation of MA63, particularly by ensuring that federal legislative powers are conferred on the Sarawak government in an orderly and effective manner, in accordance with Article 95C of the Federal Constitution,” he said in a statement today.

Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the amendment was a crucial step before the application of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (Act 127) is suspended in Sarawak to enable the state government to assume responsibility for scheduled waste management.
The move, he said, would also prevent overlapping jurisdiction between the federal and Sarawak governments.
Fahmi also said the transfer of federal legislative powers in environmental matters to Sabah and Sarawak would be implemented in phases, beginning with scheduled waste management, he added.

“The Government remains committed to translating the MA63 agenda into concrete actions and decisions to strengthen federal-state relations and safeguard the interests of the people of Sabah and Sarawak,” he said. — Bernama
416e4491e7f5674c: KUALA LUMPUR: Singer and actress Linda Rafar has shared an emotional tribute to her late son, Rezaimen Keiflin Keifli, as the family prepares for the wedding of her eldest surviving son, Rezaril Keifli, this weekend.
In a heartfelt Instagram post, Linda addressed Rezaimen, affectionately known as Memen, to share that his younger brother, Aril, is getting married tomorrow.
She said she was certain Memen would have been delighted to witness the occasion.
"Memen, Mama wants to tell you something. Aril is getting married. Mama is so happy. If you were here, you would surely be happy to see your best friend getting married, wouldn't you?" she wrote.
The former Elite member admitted that the approaching nuptials had stirred mixed feelings, leaving her overjoyed for Rezaril while deeply grieved by the longing for the child she lost.
"If only Memen were here, everything would feel complete. He would surely be busy with Aril, joking around and celebrating his happy day alongside his other siblings," she said.
Rezaimen passed away in July 2014 at the age of 12 following a battle with a chronic abdominal tumour.
He was Linda's son from her first marriage to former race car driver Keifli Othman.
She later married actor Syed Aiman in 2006, with whom she has three sons.
Linda added that she was trying to stay strong while continuing with the wedding preparations, despite knowing her late son's absence would leave an irreplaceable void.
She expressed hope that the wedding would go smoothly and prayed for strength to navigate the emotional days ahead.
"Mama misses you, Memen. I miss you so much," she added.
Rezaril, 26, will tie the knot with his fiancée, Nur Izzati Syafikah, fondly known as Ika, in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, tomorrow.
Linda previously shared that his decision to marry had moved the entire family to tears, noting how rarely she had been apart from him since his infancy.

73fed04d79ec0ac3: The autofill feature of Apple's Safari browser appears to be suffering from a date handling error that occasionally leads it to supply an incorrect credit card expiration date when filling out forms.

The supposed issue has been a sore spot for Apple customers dating back at least to 2017, when the author of an Apple Community forum post complained about changes to the month field in the Autofill credit card expiration date when moving between time zones.

"I've noticed for the last year or so, whenever I travel from Eastern time zone (my home) to Central time zone or even Pacific time zone that my credit card expiration date month changes in Safari Autofill," the Safari user wrote.
Another post in 2021 raised similar concerns.

"I don't know how to reproduce this," the author wrote. "Every few months Safari on any of my devices changes the expiration month of all of my stored credit cards by decreasing the month by 1, for example instead of 10/2029 it changes it to 09/2029."
Three years later, another person posting to Apple's Community forum reported the same issue.

"For a few years now every time I use Autofill on my computer my credit cards (ALL of them) always have their expiration dates change one month earlier," the 2024 post says. "I thought it was just a glitch on my computer but I bought a new computer and didn't transfer anything from my old one and it is still doing it."
An unrelated Autofill bug report from 2024 suggests that if there is an issue, it resides in Apple-owned Safari code rather than Safari's open source WebKit engine.

Wherever the bug may reside, Safari's unreliable handling of credit card dates has kept a complaint-filled Reddit thread going for four years. And the reported month-shifting has been noted in other threads, too.
The Register was unable to reproduce the described behavior, but a reader insists it's still a problem.
"The Safari AutoFill feature sometimes fills in the credit card expiration date wrong," the reader explained. "My credit card expires in December, but sometimes Apple helpfully enters November."
"To be clear, the card is stored correctly when inspected in Settings," our tipster added. "The off-by-one error only happens when filling out a form in Safari, and not consistently."

One possible way this might happen is if the Safari Autofill code implemented the expiration date using Swift's DateComponent type and stored it as a Calendar object with UTC as the TimeZone identifier. Doing so would anchor the date to a specific time. If the date components were extracted in Pacific Time, the value would be represented as eight hours ahead (PST). So 9/1/2027 at 00:00 would appear as 8/31/2027 at 16:00.

Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but we're told Apple's Help Desk – or "Helpless Desk" as our source put it – advised clearing the browser cache and re-entering details of the affected credit card.
If that works, it suggests Safari's handling of cached data in the context of Autofill dates may need to be revisited.
Apple does not maintain a public bug database and the community-maintained OpenRadar sheds no light on these reports. ®

85122dc1d0927797: NEW DELHI, Nov 6 — India’s cricket board has moved an international match scheduled for December out of New Delhi because of “potential weather disruption”, as air pollution levels surged in the city.
Toxic air pollution in the megacity spiked on Friday to more than 25 times the World Health Organization’s recommended daily limit, data from air monitors showed.
The southeastern coastal city of Visakhapatnam will instead host the one-day international (ODI) match between India and Sri Lanka on December 13.
The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) said the decision was made “in view of the potential weather disruption and the proposed renovation work” at the Delhi stadium.
During winter pollution peaks, when colder air traps pollutants close to the ground, PM2.5 readings can exceed 800 micrograms per cubic metre — more than 50 times the WHO’s 24-hour guideline.

Air pollution was linked to an estimated 17,188 deaths in Delhi in 2023, nearly 15 per cent of the total, making it the city’s biggest individual risk factor, an analysis by Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) found.
Pollution is expected to worsen on Sunday during Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, when fireworks displays add to the already poisonous air. — AFP
1e8081cefba918d3: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is monitoring the possible impact of the recent US election results on tariffs and bilateral trade relations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the cabinet had discussed the short- and medium-term implications of the Republican Party's electoral setbacks.
"As for whether this will affect tariffs and other matters, we are still monitoring developments," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Taman Kosas in Ampang today.
Anwar said Malaysia would continue engaging with President Donald Trump's administration, as well as existing and newly elected members of the US Congress.
He described the election results as an internal matter for the US but welcomed what he saw as a rejection of racial and religious hatred.
"Personally, I am pleased with these developments and changes because of the message they send.
"The message is against violence and racial hatred," he said.
He said the results reflected public dissatisfaction with political rhetoric targeting minority communities, including Muslims.
He expressed hope that the developments would help ease international geopolitical tensions.
He said Malaysia should also learn from the importance of rejecting racial hatred and focusing on good governance.
"What matters for us in Malaysia is to teach people to be good human beings and to cleanse the country of greed and corruption," he said.
The US midterm elections held on Tuesday saw Democrats wrest control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives from Trump's Republican Party.
d2c692c1605a7de9: MELAKA: Melaka police recorded 172 arrests in 24 raids targeting increasingly complex commercial crime syndicates, particularly call centre operations, between January and October this year.

State police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said 20 investigation papers had led to charges being filed in court, following continued enforcement by the state Commercial Crime Investigation Department.
He said the National Scam Response Centre 997 recorded 591 investigation papers during the same period, of which 289 cases were resolved, representing a resolution rate of 48.90 per cent.
Of the cases resolved, 60 had been brought to court, 10 were classified as no further action, while 219 were classified as temporary updates.
Dzulkhairi said police had also seized RM424,766 in efforts to recover money lost by scam victims.
Of the amount seized, RM174,793.43 had been returned to victims in 49 cases, representing a recovery rate of 41.15 per cent, he said in a statement posted on the Melaka police official Facebook page.

085996030dba122c: SINGAPORE, Nov 6 — Singapore and Malaysia will increase the quota of licensed cross-border taxis from 300 to 500 per country from November 16, 2026, while allowing two additional ride-hailing operators to provide services under the enhanced Cross-Border Taxi Scheme.
A joint statement by the transport ministries of both countries said the two new operators, CDG Zig Pte Ltd and Kumpool Sdn Bhd, would also be licensed to operate under the scheme from the same date.
“Commuters and drivers can look forward to more options for cross-border point-to-point trips, greater convenience and a better commuting experience,” said the statement on Friday.

According to the joint statement, the developments reflect the continued commitment of Singapore and Malaysia to strengthening cross-border connectivity and improving the commuting experience for travellers between the two countries.
“The improvements will further strengthen the strong business linkages and people-to-people ties between Singapore and Malaysia,” it said.

Meanwhile, Land Public Transport Agency of Malaysia (APAD) Director-General Ahmad Radhi Ma’arof said Malaysia welcomed the expansion of the taxi quota and the addition of two licensed platform operators.
“... this shows a significant milestone in enhancing the cross-border passenger movement to complement the first-mile-last-mile connectivity between Johor Bahru, Malaysia and Singapore.
“It is our hope that this new development will signify further enhancement of connectivity between the two great nations,” he said.
The two new ride-hailing operators — CDG Zig and Kumpool — will join GrabCar Pte Ltd as licensed operators under the Cross-Border Taxi Scheme.

“The increase in quota is an important step towards strengthening cross-border connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia, and reflects the strong and longstanding cooperation between our two countries,” said Singapore Land Transport Authority Chief Executive, Ng Lang.

“By expanding the availability of licensed cross-border services, we are giving travellers more options and greater flexibility for their journeys. We will continue to work closely with our Malaysian counterparts to improve cross-border travel and better serve the needs of travellers in both countries,” said Ng.

On May 4, 2026, Singapore and Malaysia introduced enhancements to the Cross-Border Taxi Scheme to bring greater convenience to travellers while ensuring fair operating conditions for transport providers and drivers in both countries.

The measures include new designated pick-up points for ride-hailing and e-hailing bookings, more flexible drop-off points, an increase in the quota of licensed cross-border taxis and additional requirements to support enforcement against illegal domestic point-to-point trips. — Bernama
6adcd8c80688bfec: TAIPEI: Taiwan ordered the financial regulator on Friday to "stabilise" the stock market, as the island's tech-heavy index was caught up in a massive sell-off hitting global markets.
Shares in Taiwanese chipmaking giant TSMC plummeted as much as 9.8%, dragging the Taiex as much as 9% lower during trading.

Investors in tech stocks were spooked by a collapse on Wall Street fuelled by fears that US Democrats will ramp up regulation of the artificial intelligence industry following their blowout victory in the midterm elections.

Premier Cho Jung-tai said he had told the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) to "closely monitor developments in both international and domestic stock markets and to remain flexible in determining how to stabilise the domestic market".
"Whenever the Financial Supervisory Commission has faced unusually severe stock market volatility in the past, it has always implemented relevant response measures," Cho told reporters.
Cho added that Taiwan's economic fundamentals were sound and "the profitability and potential of our various industries remain quite robust".
The FSC will meet on Friday to decide on measures to stabilise the market, the Commercial Times newspaper reported.
Taiwanese people have piled into the local stock market this year as it has soared to record highs on booming demand for AI technology.
At the close, the Taiex was down 4.5% at 39,690.7.
9c1d149b7da57929: AMPANG: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says he disagrees with Umno paying Najib Razak’s RM50 million fine, which has paved the way for the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his graft conviction under house arrest.

Former Umno president Najib was granted a house arrest order by the Kuala Lumpur High Court today after Umno paid his RM50 million fine using funds collected through a donation drive launched in September.
“My personal view is that I disagree with this as it could give the public the impression that large-scale corruption can go unpunished,” Anwar told reporters after Friday prayers here.
Umno secretary-general Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki announced earlier today that the party had settled the fine through funds raised from a donation drive launched in September.
Najib’s lawyer Farhan Shafee later confirmed that the fine had been paid, and he would deliver the house arrest order to Kajang prison – where Najib has been held since 2022.
Najib was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC International funds.
He was sentenced to 12 years' jail and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, a royal pardon halved his prison sentence and reduced his fine to RM50 million.

In September this year, the current Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The release was subject to Najib's payment of the RM50 million fine and his compliance with other conditions.
2173951b94563c70: SHAH ALAM: The Klang Royal City Council (MBDK) has urged residents in low-lying and riverbank areas to prepare for a five-day high-tide phenomenon starting tomorrow.
Mayor Datuk Abd Hamid Hussain advised residents to monitor official weather advisories and avoid high-risk zones during heavy rain and high tides.
"Important documents and valuables should be kept in a safe place, vehicles moved to higher ground, and families should ensure they have sufficient emergency supplies," he said in a statement today.
According to the Klang District Disaster Management Committee, the high-tide phenomenon will run until Nov 11, with water levels at the Port Klang station forecast to hit 5.2m.
The peak tide is expected at 5.02am on Sunday, placing it in the warning category.
Under Port Klang water level guidelines, readings between 5m and 5.3m fall within the warning category, while levels from 5.4m to 5.5m enter the danger category.
The committee said thunderstorms are expected in several areas on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, with rain forecast in parts of the district at night.
Abd Hamid said MBDK was prepared for potential floods and high tides through coordinated measures with relevant agencies.

He said the council was focusing on several flood-prone spots, including the Bukit Raja intersection, Taman Mutiara Bukit Raja, Taman Melawis, Kampung Bukit Kapar, Taman Meru Indah, Taman Seri Kerayong, Taman Daya Maju, and Jalan Haji Salleh in Pekan Meru.
"Priority is being given to upgrading drainage systems, installing flap gates, repairing discharge pipes and maintaining retention ponds.
"The MBDK Rapid Response Squad and relevant departments remain on high alert to ensure a swift response to any complaints or disaster-related incidents," he said.
Abd Hamid said the council received 83 disaster-related complaints over two days starting Wednesday, with 62 resolved, 16 under action, and five involving special assistance.
He said residents whose vehicles or properties were damaged by fallen trees within MBDK's jurisdiction could submit compensation claims to the council.
"A police report must first be lodged before any claim is submitted for review and further action," he said. — BERNAMA

421ee6e5a5da6bad: AMPANG: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim tidak setuju Umno membayar denda RM50 juta bagi membolehkan Najib Razak menjalani tahanan rumah.
Katanya, walaupun Umno mempunyai semangat persahabatan dengan Najib, perkara itu tidak seharusnya berlaku kerana memberi gambaran kepada rakyat kegiatan rasuah berskala besar boleh dibiarkan.

“Pandangan peribadi…saya tidak setuju kerana sementara kita ada semangat persahabatan dengan Najib, tapi itu tidak harus memberi gambaran kepada rakyat bahawa kegiatan rasuah yang mencecah bilion ringgit boleh dibiarkan begitu rupa,” katanya ditemui selepas solat Jumaat di Masjid Taman Kosas.
Beliau berkata, prinsip menolak penyalahgunaan kuasa dan rasuah perlu diterapkan kepada generasi muda tanpa mengira kedudukan atau hubungan seseorang.
“Apa yang kita nak didik kepada anak-anak kita? Satu prinsip akhlak yang tegas menolak penyalahgunaan kuasa dan rasuah,” katanya.
Bagaimanapun, Anwar berkata keputusan berhubung pembayaran itu terletak pada Umno, manakala proses undang-undang dan keputusan Yang di-Pertuan Agong perlu dihormati mengikut perlembagaan.

“Dan soal keputusan Umno itu hak mereka dan proses undang-undang kita hormat cara prosesnya ataupun dari segi keputusan yang di Yang di-Pertuan Agong, itu kita hormat dari segi perlembagaan,” katanya.

Umno hari ini mengumumkan kutipan menerusi Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak sudah mencapai sasaran dan mencukupi untuk membayar denda RM50 juta itu. Setiausaha Agungnya, Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki turut mengesahkan semua urusan pembayaran kepada Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur selesai.

Tabung itu dilancarkan pada 18 Sept lalu selepas Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan memberikan pengampunan bersyarat kepada Najib, yang membolehkannya menjalani baki hukuman penjara menerusi tahanan di rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028, tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda RM50 juta.
d5cd5a25da0e7139: FIUMICINO: Pope Leo XIV headed to South America on Friday for an emotionally charged reunion with the continent that helped shape his priesthood, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery.

The 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church will in 12 days visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in one of the most intense papal foreign trips in decades, meeting political leaders, prisoners, and the poor, as well as old friends.
A smiling Leo waved to onlookers before boarding his plane under overcast skies at Rome's Fiumicino airport, with the aircraft taking off shortly after 0600 GMT, according to AFP journalists.

The Church's first US-born pope served for almost two decades in Peru as a missionary, forming a deep attachment to the continent. Leo said on Wednesday that he was looking forward to returning to those countries "so dear to me".

The head of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics said he hoped the trip would "strengthen faith, renew hope, and rekindle the fire of charity" in the countries, which share challenges from rising inequality and violence to demographic falls and the decline of Catholicism.

Despite undergoing an operation on Oct 13 to remove a cancerous tumour, doctors have given him the all-clear to travel, and the Vatican said no special medical measures were necessary beyond the standard care on papal trips.
Secular Uruguay

Leo begins his trip in Uruguay, Latin America's most secular country – and one of the wealthiest – where a tight security operation is in place, with some 5,000 police officers and 1,000 soldiers mobilised.
He will be driven along Montevideo's waterfront promenade in a custom-made popemobile before meeting left-wing president Yamandu Orsi and receiving the keys to the city.
"I have family members who plan to go to the waterfront to watch him pass," Janet Rodríguez, 47, told AFP.
"I won't be going, as I'm not religious. But it's great that someone of such importance is coming," she said.

Cardinal Daniel Sturla, archbishop of Montevideo, told AFP there was "widespread interest in the pope's visit that goes well beyond the confines of the Catholic Church", with tickets for masses in Paysandu and Florida quickly running out.

The liberal nation is at odds with the centuries-old institution on same-sex marriage, abortion and euthanasia – which was legalised last year – and Leo is expected to appeal to protect life as well as traditional family values.

Uruguay has the highest suicide rate in Latin America, and the pope may talk about mental health, particularly when visiting the Casavalle neighbourhood in Montevideo, notorious for high levels of poverty and extreme violence.
'Symbolism and emotion'
The pope will travel Sunday to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor, Pope Francis, who disappointed many Argentinians by not returning to visit during his papacy.
Leo's trip is seen as a double homecoming of sorts, US-based Vatican expert Christopher White told AFP.
"History's first Latin American pope, Francis, never returned to his homeland. Leo, a Peruvian citizen, now carries forward that mantle and legacy," said White, author of a book on Pope Leo.
The South America trip culminates in Peru, and Leo's arrival there on Wednesday will be "a moment full of symbolism and emotion", he said.

The country has been gripped by pope fever. In Lima, vendors are selling T-shirts and rosaries with his image on them, while Leo bread is on sale in bakeries. Inmates in a women's prison are crafting dolls in his likeness.
A towering, 14-metre (46-foot) statue of Leo has also been erected in the port city of Callao, which he is to visit.

The trip will take him to the former Inca capital of Cusco and the Amazon rainforest, but the pope will also revisit his former life as Robert Francis Prevost, from a supper with priests from his old diocese of Chiclayo to a private visit to a chapel he helped rebuild.
b714f4804bbe9530: PUTRAJAYA: Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation pledge has come back into focus following former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's release from Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

870ccc5684f31911: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will continue to welcome investment from China and other countries despite concerns raised by the United States over competition in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor investments.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had contacted him to discuss preparations for a possible meeting with President Donald Trump in Manila or Shanghai.
He said Washington wanted to ensure that American investment opportunities, particularly in AI and chips, were not undermined by other countries.
"Their concern is that opportunities for American investment, especially in AI and chips, should not be disrupted by any other country.
"I told him that we do not interfere in the decisions of individual countries," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Taman Kosas in Ampang today.
Anwar said Malaysia would provide opportunities for American investors without restricting investment from China or other countries.
"We give space to the United States, but that does not mean restricting China's activities or those of other countries here," he said.
He cited Google's US$15 billion investment, which he said would be accelerated over the next two years.
However, Anwar said investors must meet Malaysia's requirements, including providing their own water supply, training and university-related facilities.
He said the same principle applied to rare earth investments, with Malaysia remaining open to participation from any country.
However, investors must process the minerals domestically, comply with local regulations and ensure the materials were not used to manufacture weapons that could threaten national security.
"We give opportunities to any country, but the conditions are that processing must take place within the country and local regulations must be followed," he said.
Earlier, Anwar and Rubio discussed ways to expand economic cooperation under the upgraded Malaysia-US Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP).
Bilateral trade between Malaysia and the US rose 25.7 per cent to RM235.19 billion in the first six months of 2026 compared with the same period last year.

25000554e4e526e0: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim disagrees with Umno's decision to pay Datuk Seri Najib Razak's RM50 million fine but says it is the party's right to do so.
"If Umno wants to pay RM50 million, that is its decision. That is its business.

"Personally, I disagree because while we maintain a spirit of friendship with Umno, it should not give the impression that corruption involving billions of ringgit can simply be overlooked," he told reporters after Friday prayers.
The settling of Najib's RM50 million fine paves the way for him to serve the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest.
Anwar said Malaysians must uphold firm moral principles against corruption and abuse of power.
"What do we want to teach our children? A strong moral principle that rejects abuse of power and corruption," he said.
He stressed that Umno had the right to make its own decisions and that the legal process and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's constitutional powers must be respected.
"As for Umno's decision, that is their right. We respect the legal process and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's prerogative to grant clemency under the Constitution.
"I have already expressed my personal view," he said.
Earlier today, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki confirmed that the party had completed payment of Najib's RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
He said the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, launched on Sept 18, had collected sufficient donations to settle the fine.

The payment fulfils a key condition of the royal pardon granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Sept 18, allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib's lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee confirmed that the High Court had issued a house arrest order following the payment.
He said the legal team would deliver the order to Kajang Prison, although further administrative procedures were required before Najib could be transferred home.
The date of his transfer has yet to be confirmed.
Under the conditional pardon, Najib must comply with the stipulated conditions or risk having the pardon revoked and serving the remainder of his sentence in prison.
Najib has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds.
He was originally sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment and fined RM210 million, but the Pardons Board reduced his sentence to six years and the fine to RM50 million in January 2024.
de1b721ce58c1616: KUALA SELANGOR: Kerajaan Selangor akan mengarahkan semakan semula terhadap projek pembangunan yang diluluskan bagi memastikan pelaksanaan penyediaan sistem mitigasi banjir di kawasan berisiko.
Menteri Besar, Amirudin Shari, berkata langkah itu antara usaha kerajaan negeri bagi memastikan risiko banjir dapat dikurangkan serta kejadian sama tidak berulang di kawasan terjejas.

“Saya akan minta semak balik segala kelulusan yang telah kita benarkan termasuk mensyaratkan mereka (pemaju) membuat tadahan air sementara (dan) kita juga tidak mahu mereka melakukannya secara sambil lewa,” katanya.
Amirudin berkata demikian ketika ditemui selepas meninjau lokasi kolam tadahan di Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Kampus Puncak Alam, hari ini.
Beliau berkata, kerajaan negeri turut mengenal pasti beberapa isu lain yang menyumbang kepada kejadian banjir di kawasan seperti Johan Setia, Parit Mahang, Bukit Kuching dan Bukit Hijau.

Katanya, antara isu itu ialah aktiviti vandalisme di ban Rancangan Tebatan Banjir (RTB) Sungai Buloh 1 yang menyebabkan ia menjadi lebih rendah daripada spesifikasi asal di sesetengah bahagian selain limpahan daripada Lebuhraya Pantai Barat (WCE).
“Saya sudah minta isu vandalisme ditangani dengan segera dan kita akan ambil tindakan terhadap operasi haram di sana, dan ada beberapa proses perobohan yang terpaksa dilakukan.

“Perobohan itu untuk jadikan gazet kawasan tadahan air atau dataran banjir di dua tempat yang kita kenal pasti yang akan dilaksanakan oleh Pejabat Daerah dan Tanah dengan kerjasama pihak berkuasa tempatan,” katanya.

Dalam pada itu, mengenai sebuah masjid di sini yang sering dilanda banjir, Amirudin berkata pihaknya akan berbincang dengan pihak pentadbiran masjid sama ada untuk meninggikan atau memindahkan masjid itu kerana kawasan terbabit ialah kawasan rendah dan menerima limpahan Sungai Subang.

“Itu (banjir) ialah limpahan Sungai Subang yang mengalir ke Merbau Sempak, Sungai Buloh dan akhirnya sampai ke sini. Itu pergerakan air sejak dahulu, dari Gombak atau Petaling dan sebahagiannya ke kawasan Ijok atau Kuala Selangor,” katanya.

d17738979dd45f86: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional election machinery for the Melaka polls must not become complacent or overconfident about voter support, as voting patterns can change at any time, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said.
He said the results of previous elections showed that voter support was not necessarily permanent, and that any changes in voting patterns should be taken seriously.
Party workers must continue working hard to engage with voters and not assume BN candidates' victories are guaranteed based solely on the party's strength or past performance.
"Do not be too confident that our candidates will win, as voter patterns can change at any time.
"Before the last general election, BN won many seats in Melaka and we managed to form the state government.

70838a2d72ac3386: Welcome to Friday and therefore to a fresh edition of On Call, The Register's weekly tale of tech support trials and tribulations that readers kindly share.
This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Mason," who told us he once worked at a hospital doing tech support for its research labs.
"One of the labs was for a doctor who was one of the world's top organ transplant researchers" Mason told On Call.
The doctor was also a voracious consumer of – ahem – adult entertainment, a habit that saw his PC and other machines around the lab often come down with a nasty case of malware.
Mason got to clean that up, sometimes multiple times in a single week.
The doctor's foibles were widely known around the hospital, as was the fact that his activities violated several workplace policies.
Mason pointed this out to his boss every time he cleaned up a fresh malware outbreak but such was the doctor's status that management never intervened.

And then the hospital was hit by a nasty cyber-worm that did a lot of damage. During the cleanup, Mason's colleagues found logs that showed the doctor's PC was the source of the infection, and that he had been indulging in his online hobby at the time the worm arrived.
Mason assumed this would be the moment at which the doctor would finally be held accountable and face disciplinary action.

Instead the doctor made a bargain with the IT department to henceforth use only a designated PC when pursuing – ahem – personal and/or intimate matters. And he would only use office PCs for actual work.
The hospital's tech team rescued a PC from its e-waste pile for this job.
"Get this thing going and deliver it to Doctor Pervert," Mason's boss ordered.

By this stage, Mason had had enough. He escalated his protests, telling his boss that indulging this doctor was unprofessional, likely exposed the hospital to lawsuits, wasted IT department resources, and was just wrong.
"What do you want to hear?" his boss replied. "The CIO told me do this or get another job."
After Mason prepped that PC, he only needed to clean up malware about once a year – after the poor machine was so overrun with malware that it no longer served the doctor's purposes.
Mason left the hospital while this PC was still in place.

"You'll be shocked, no doubt, to learn that years later the doctor's graduate students filed a lawsuit," he told On Call. "And that the separate fun-time computer was one of the pieces of evidence that the hospital knew about his – ahem – proclivities and not just ignored them but facilitated them."

Have you been asked to cover up revolting behavior? Or ignore policy? Click here to share your story with On Call. It's our policy to tell a great tech support story week, so we appreciate every contribution. ®

1e8fcfffb748ab08: NOVEMBER 6 — More than a century after Vincent van Gogh painted one of the world’s most celebrated masterpieces, scientific research is offering a fascinating new perspective on the night sky that may have inspired it. For generations, Vincent van Gogh’s The Starry Night has captivated audiences with its swirling skies, luminous stars and extraordinary sense of movement.
But what if the celestial arrangement in this iconic painting was inspired by an actual morning sky?

A study published in Scientific Reports, part of the Nature Portfolio, explores precisely this possibility. Using astronomical simulations, historical records and mathematical analysis, researchers reconstructed the sky over Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France, where Van Gogh was staying in 1889.
For generations, Vincent van Gogh’s ‘The Starry Night’ has captivated audiences with its swirling skies, luminous stars and extraordinary sense of movement. — Google Art Project pic
Their findings suggest that the arrangement of the Moon, Venus and the Hyades star cluster on July 22, 1889 closely resembles elements of the celestial composition depicted in the painting.
Can we see the beauty of the universe in the microscopic world of cells?

From a biological perspective, this discovery invites an interesting comparison between the vastness of the cosmos and the microscopic world of living cells. Look at stars and galaxies through a telescope, then observe cells and their intricate structures under a microscope. Both reveal fascinating patterns, clusters, networks and complexity. Despite their unimaginable differences in scale, they remind us of the extraordinary ways nature creates and organises its structures, from the architecture of a single cell to the vastness of the universe.

As a cancer immunologist, this parallel offers another way of appreciating the beauty of science. The cellular world, much like the night sky, holds patterns and interactions that are not always visible to the naked eye. Sometimes, it takes a different lens to discover the extraordinary within what initially appears ordinary.

The researchers combined astronomy with art history to investigate the possible origins of Van Gogh’s masterpiece. Their findings offer another perspective on how observation and imagination can come together to create something extraordinary.

Importantly, the study does not establish the definitive date on which the painting was completed. Rather, it presents a compelling scientific hypothesis about the sky that may have inspired its creation.

More than 137 years later, The Starry Night continues to reveal new dimensions of its beauty. From the vastness of the cosmos to the microscopic architecture of a cell, perhaps nature has always been creating art in patterns we are only beginning to understand. Sometimes, all it takes is a different lens to discover that the universe and the microscopic world are not so different after all.

* The author is a University Lecturer at Pusat Kanser Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, Universiti Sains Malaysia and Visiting Scientist at the International Agency for Research on Cancer, World Health Organisation.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

506759cb7a0a36a5: WASHINGTON: A judge temporarily blocked construction of President Donald Trump's proposed 76-metre triumphal arch in Washington from beginning late on Thursday, shortly after it won a key approval.

US District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a 14-day restraining order following an 8-4 vote by the National Capital Planning Commission to approve the project, after it heard from about 100 opponents, including Democratic lawmakers.
The Trump administration contends that Congress approved the arch more than 100 years ago when it also authorised construction of a bridge across the Potomac River.

"The sheer improbability that a 100-year-old statute would contain authority, unknown to every previous administration, to erect a 250-foot arch at a principal location in the nation's capital indicates how far (the government) must stretch to justify this project," Chutkan wrote.
She said approval would result in about three years of construction "that will disrupt traffic, create noise, result in large-scale excavation, and more".

The Justice Department had said earlier that, if the project was approved, it expected an initial six to eight months of construction focused on excavation and foundation work to begin as soon as Thursday. Above-ground construction would start in May 2027 at the earliest, with the job expected to take 33 to 39 months in total.

"It will snarl traffic for years, impact the nearby airport, and present even more serious threats to public safety that this commission has refused to acknowledge and grapple with," said Representative Don Beyer, a Democrat who represents northern Virginia.
The National Park Service also said late on Thursday that it had approved the project.

The arch is among several costly projects Trump is pushing in Washington despite opposition from local officials and conservationists. They include rebuilding the Reflecting Pool at the Lincoln Memorial, constructing a massive White House ballroom and overhauling the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.

The arch has faced significant opposition in the courts. The state of Virginia and the District of Columbia sued the National Park Service and the Department of the Interior on Saturday, seeking to halt the start of construction, calling it "legally indefensible" and arguing that Congress had not approved it.
They also raised a number of concerns about the project's impact on traffic.
At an event on Monday to highlight improvements to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, Trump said the arch would also serve as a military asset and would be able to house drones and snipers.
"It's right smack in the middle of everything, so very important for our military. But from a beautification standpoint, it'll be the most beautiful arch in the world," Trump said.

The arch, which would include an eternal flame and floodlights to make it visible to pilots, would be situated across the Potomac River from the Lincoln Memorial, on a highway roundabout near the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery.

It would resemble the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, but stand more than 80 feet taller. It would also be nearly as tall as the US Capitol, which, at 288 feet, can be seen across much of Washington. The site is near the final approach path for aircraft landing at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.
A rendering showed the flame would be held by a 60-foot-tall gold, winged female figure positioned atop the arch and flanked by gold flying eagles.
Critics say it would cast shadows over some graves at Arlington National Cemetery, while the Trump administration said it would honour veterans.

4ad2f45f9337640f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The High Court has issued a house arrest order for Datuk Seri Najib Razak after his RM50 million fine in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case was settled today.
Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, a member of Najib’s legal team, confirmed the payment was made by Umno to the High Court registry this morning, according to The Star.

d86fdfa2e28ec439: KUALA LUMPUR: The immigration department has busted a syndicate believed to have raked in up to RM15,000 a month by forging immigration endorsement security stamps, following the arrest of three people on Tuesday.

Immigration director-general Zakaria Shaaban said the operation was carried out by the intelligence and special operations division of the department's headquarters in Putrajaya following a month of surveillance of two residential premises.

He said the three suspects, comprising a Malaysian man and two Thai women aged 40 to 45, were believed to be the syndicate's mastermind and members. They were arrested in Kajang, Selangor, and Pandan Perdana here.

"Preliminary checks revealed that one of the Thai women holds a long-term social visit pass as the spouse of a Malaysian citizen, while the other holds a social visit pass,” he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said the syndicate forged immigration endorsement security stamps to make them appear to have been issued at the Sultan Iskandar Building entry point at Bukit Chagar, Johor Bahru.
The syndicate targeted foreign nationals, particularly Thai nationals, who were staying in the country without valid passes or had overstayed.

“The syndicate is believed to have promoted its services through WhatsApp, charging clients between RM70 and RM100 for each forged immigration endorsement security stamp placed in their passports," he said.
He said their clients only needed to submit their passports without meeting syndicate members in person to avoid detection.

The items seized during the operation included two forged visit pass endorsement stamps, one forged exit endorsement stamp, two rubber stamps bearing forged endorsements, two date stamps, and five red-and-blue ink pads.
Also seized were six Thai passports, a Thai border pass, five mobile phones, two notebooks, and keys to the premises.

4a373ce46c94e080: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 6 — The Johor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) has recorded 2,373 offences, with seizures amounting to over RM11.6 million, from the start of the year until yesterday.
Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said that of this total, 1,774 cases involved offences under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011.

She said among the offences were the failure to display clear price tags or price lists for goods or services, selling controlled items above the stipulated maximum price and raising prices or profiteering in an unreasonable manner.

“During the same period, Johor KPDN also recorded 360 offences under the Weights and Measures Act 1972, 119 cases under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and 66 offences under the Consumer Protection Act 1999,” she said during a state-level Festive Season Maximum Price Scheme (SHMMP) launch in conjunction with Deepavali 2026 at NSK Trade City in Skudai here today.
Lilis Saslinda said the ministry also detected 54 other offences under the Trademarks Act 2019, the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, the Copyright Act 1987 and the Hire-Purchase Act 1967.

She noted that 879 offences were also detected out of 1,537 inspections conducted at the wholesale and retail levels during the implementation of the SHMMP for this year’s Chinese New Year and Hari Raya Aidilfitri celebrations.
Lilis Saslinda said the most frequently detected offense was the failure to display the required pink price tags for controlled items.

She urged traders to adhere to four key obligations during the SHMMP implementation: not selling controlled items above the maximum price, displaying pink price tags for controlled items, ensuring an adequate supply of goods in the market, and using approved weighing instruments and measuring scales.
“The Johor chapter of the ministry has taken proactive measures by intensifying advocacy efforts directed at traders.

“These were made through announcements on official social media channels, the distribution of leaflets on the list of controlled goods, as well as the responsibilities and obligations of traders,” she said.
